title: Xanthe and the Vector
premise: Ivo Nystrom has spent eleven years alone on Relay Station Vesper, tending a beacon whose original purpose was purged from every archive he can access. When the ship Cassiopeia returns from a forty-year deep-space survey with its crew biologically younger than when they left—victims of an experimental cryo-reversal protocol—Ivo learns the beacon he maintains is the anchor point for a fleet-wide decision: only half of humanity's frozen sleepers can be revived before the station's failing power core dies. Among the reversed crew is Dr. Xanthe Adeyemi, the engineer who designed the beacon and Ivo's forgotten first love, her memories of him intact while his were traded away as payment for his posting. As factions aboard the Cassiopeia fight over who deserves waking, Ivo and Xanthe must reconstruct their shared past and choose: save the crew she loves or the strangers history forgot. In the end, Ivo sacrifices his own revival slot and uploads his memories into the beacon itself, becoming the station's living archive so that both halves of humanity can wake—and Xanthe wakes to a world where he exists everywhere and nowhere.
about_author: Freya Okonkwo is a former radio astronomer who spent three years at a remote observatory in the Atacama Desert before turning to fiction. She writes about isolation, machines that outlive their makers, and the stubborn arithmetic of love.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A day in his meticulously ordered routine on Station Vesper: calibrating the beacon, logging anomalies nobody reads, talking to the maintenance drones. He admits, almost fondly, that he no longer remembers why he volunteered. Emotional beat: loneliness worn so long it feels like peace.

chapters.title: Signal Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ivo detects a return ping on a frequency decommissioned decades ago—the beacon answering something that shouldn't exist. His logs show he queried it once, years ago, and cannot recall doing so. Emotional beat: the first hairline crack in his certainty about his own past.

chapters.title: Cassiopeia Returns
chapters.summary: A battered survey ship decelerates into range, broadcasting a crew manifest Ivo recognizes from pre-departure records. Docking protocols engage automatically, as if the station expected them. Emotional beat: dread and hunger for company arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: Younger Than Their Files
chapters.summary: Ivo meets the crew: nine people biologically twenty years younger than their service records. Their commander, Okafor, is evasive about the reversal protocol. One crew member stares at Ivo like she knows him. Emotional beat: uncanny hospitality between strangers who aren't strangers.

chapters.title: Xanthe
chapters.summary: Xanthe Adeyemi's POV. She recognizes Ivo instantly—the man who gave up his memories to take this posting so she could keep hers. She says nothing, testing whether anything in him still turns toward her. Emotional beat: grief disguised as restraint.

chapters.title: The Reversal Protocol
chapters.summary: Okafor briefs Ivo: the deep-space mission tested cryo-reversal, and it worked—but it drained the relay network's power grid. The beacon is now the last node capable of reviving humanity's frozen sleepers, and only half of them. Emotional beat: the weight of an arithmetic with no remainder.

chapters.title: What the Core Remembers
chapters.summary: Ivo descends into the station's power core and finds physical archives the network purge missed: schematics signed by Xanthe, and a maintenance contract bearing his own signature dated before he remembers existing. Emotional beat: vertigo of a self with missing floors.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Hunger
chapters.summary: Shared dinner scene. The crew debates revival criteria—skills, genetics, lottery—while Xanthe watches Ivo fail to remember a joke only the two of them ever told. Emotional beat: laughter curdling into faction lines.

chapters.title: Faction Lines
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The crew splits: engineers want to wake specialists who can rebuild civilization; others demand a random draw as the only justice. Okafor quietly plans to seize the beacon console. Emotional beat: idealism hardening into coup.

chapters.title: The Memory Trade
chapters.summary: Xanthe tells Ivo the truth: memory extraction paid for his posting; his past sits in the beacon's buffer, degraded but recoverable. She offers to restore it. He refuses—afraid of becoming someone who abandons the man he is now. Emotional beat: love offered as a key he won't turn.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone vents the core's coolant reserves. Ivo traces the fault to Okafor's faction, buying time but burning half the station's remaining margin. Emotional beat: betrayal by people he'd just learned to need.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Logs
chapters.summary: Reading his own daily logs aloud to Xanthe, Ivo finds messages embedded in the metadata—a conversation with his former self, who predicted exactly this choice and begged him to choose differently. Emotional beat: intimacy with a stranger wearing your name.

chapters.title: The Lottery Proposal
chapters.summary: Ivo proposes a compromise: the beacon can split its capacity, waking half by merit and half by lot—if someone manually stabilizes the core during transfer, a likely fatal task. Everyone looks away. Emotional beat: the room learning what its conscience costs.

chapters.title: Volunteer
chapters.summary: Ivo privately begins training the drones to run the stabilization sequence without him, hiding the work inside routine maintenance. Xanthe notices the falsified logs and confronts him. Emotional beat: tenderness weaponized into argument.

chapters.title: Okafor's Coup
chapters.summary: Okafor seizes the beacon console to force a full-merit revival, overloading the core. Ivo triggers emergency lockdown, trapping himself in the core chamber with the failing reactor. Emotional beat: duty and love finally pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: Inside the Beacon
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, fragmenting. To stabilize the core he must feed it structured data—and the richest structure aboard is his own extracted memory. He begins uploading himself, reliving his life with Xanthe as the reactor drinks it. Emotional beat: remembering and dissolving as one act.

chapters.title: Everything He Gave Away
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Through the beacon's interface she experiences Ivo's restored memories alongside him—first meeting, the trade, the goodbye neither filmed. She begs him to stop; he answers with a memory of her voice saying 'somebody has to stay.' Emotional beat: shared mourning inside a machine.

chapters.title: The Choice Made Twice
chapters.summary: Climax. The core stabilizes as Ivo's memories complete the upload. The beacon achieves full capacity: all sleepers can be woken, but the man who made it possible will persist only as distributed data. Okafor, broken by what he caused, surrenders command. Emotional beat: triumph priced in erasure.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: The first cryo-pods open across the network. Revived colonists step onto stations they don't recognize, greeted by drones speaking in a composite voice assembled from one man's speech patterns. Emotional beat: rebirth haunted by absence.

chapters.title: The Archive That Answers
chapters.summary: Xanthe queries the beacon and gets responses that are unmistakably Ivo—not a recording, but something continuous, curious, and kind. Whether it's him or his echo, neither can say. Emotional beat: hope that refuses to name itself.

chapters.title: What Stays Lit
chapters.summary: Resolution. Xanthe takes the technician's post, maintaining the beacon that holds him, teaching the awakened generations the story of the man in the light. The final line mirrors the novel's first. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into vocation.

chapters.title: Vesper, Burning Steady
chapters.summary: Epilogue, years later. A child born post-revival asks the beacon a question, and it answers with a joke only two people ever told. Xanthe laughs alone in the control room. Emotional beat: love outlasting the self that carried it.
